explanations.whatIsCounted: The counter is recorded in packages/core/workspace-kernel/src/workspace-state/workspace/observation-read-view.ts, inside share(). That function wraps every read primitive of a view built by makeObservationReadView (access, stat, lstat, real-path, read-link, read-file, read-directory, read-directory-entries, decode-text, canonical-path) in withWork("axm.observation.reuse", {axm.observation.operation, axm.work.requested: 1}). A view is built only when WorkspaceReadViews.capture runs with observations: true, which happens in withWorkspaceObservationReadView and withFreshWorkspaceObservationReadView (read-view.ts). So one occurrence is one read request routed through a phase's shared view, not one executed read. Each span carries an outcome. "miss" means the wrapped fs call ran once (executed 1). "hit" or "coalesced" means a stored result was reused (executed 0, reused 1). "bypass" means the phase had ended and the call went to the live fs. In every case the underlying physical call is counted separately as axm.io.* on the instrumented adapter. The tracing guide says axm.io.* covers live reads that bypass a view, and that observation counters are logical work or reuse decisions that must not be added to physical I/O counts. So a rise in this counter means more requests now pass through a view. Whether real work rose has to be read from axm.io.*, the parse counters and the kernel recordings.
explanations.mechanism:
The main cause is commit c4f23d1be, "perf(workspace): run each post-write check in one fresh read phase". In packages/core/workspace-kernel/src/reconciliation/extensions/operations.ts, runMaterializeOperation's validate step now wraps manager.isInstalled({target}) in withFreshWorkspaceObservationReadView. In packages/core/workspace-kernel/src/reconciliation/native-output-postconditions.ts, validateNativeOutputPostconditions now runs the retention-witness check, observeNativeOutputs and the instruction readback in a single withFreshWorkspaceObservationReadView, unless there are neither retained witnesses nor required units. Before this commit both checks used independent live readers. Their stat, readlink, realpath, readdir and access calls went straight to the fs, showed up only as axm.io.*, and settings and the lockfile were decoded once per reader. Now every one of those requests goes through a fresh view and records one reuse span: a miss the first time a key is seen in the phase, a hit after that.

The phase counts line up. axm.observation.phase goes 4 -> 105 in registry/50 (100 new rows owned by axm.operation.phase: 50 presence checks plus 50 closure postconditions, one pair per restored package) and 4 -> 25 in registry/10 (20 new). Hits rise as well, for example real-path 307 -> 5,544, read-link 331 -> 5,414 and stat 151 -> 3,141. Bypass is unchanged at 11,000. The total outcome mix moves from miss 19,105 / hit 16,495 / coalesced 22 / bypass 11,000 to 98,302 / 20,108 / 22 / 11,000.

In the enable scenarios, axm.observation.phase goes 3 -> 4. explanations.whatIsCounted: It is recorded only in packages/core/workspace-kernel/src/workspace-state/workspace/read-view.ts, by cacheEvaluation and the inactive-phase bypass branch of evaluate inside WorkspaceReadViewsLive.capture. One occurrence is one call to DesiredStateReader.evaluate/graph on the reader that a read or observation phase captured (withWorkspaceReadView, withWorkspaceObservationReadView or withFreshWorkspaceObservationReadView). The call's axm.cache.outcome says what happened. On a miss (axm.work.executed=1) it runs the evaluation inside an axm.resolve.desired-state span, and that span is the executed work. On a hit (axm.work.reused-count=1) it returns the phase's cached evaluation and does no work. On a bypass it evaluates after the phase closed. So the counter counts requests (lookups) plus reuse hits, not executed work. Its executed share equals the axm.resolve.desired-state count in every rising scenario. The live DesiredStateReaderLive (desired-state-reader.ts makeDesiredStateReader) is used outside any read phase. It emits neither this kind nor axm.resolve.desired-state, only the unbounded DesiredStateReader.evaluate span, and it re-reads and re-parses axm.json and axm.lock on every call. The instrumentation itself is the same at the old revision (git show ada862c27:read-view.ts has the same withWork/bypass sites).

explanations.whatIsCounted:
There is one span "axm.observation.phase" per entry into withReadView in packages/core/workspace-kernel/src/workspace-state/workspace/read-view.ts. That code is unchanged between the two revisions. withReadView is reached through withWorkspaceReadView, withWorkspaceObservationReadView and withFreshWorkspaceObservationReadView. The span name is a traced span in apps/cli/src/cli-runtime/local-trace-policy.ts (traceSpanNames), not a member of the work vocabulary.

An occurrence takes one of two shapes:
- If a read phase is already active for the workspace location, the span is annotated axm.work.reused=true and the effect runs on the existing phase. This is a reuse hit that reads nothing.
- Otherwise it calls factory.capture() and annotates axm.work.reused=false. On exit it closes the phase with axm.work.invalidated=true and reason phase-exit. This marks the lifetime of one bounded read phase: the workspace settings and lockfile are decoded lazily, at most once each, and every reader inside shares that one view.

So the counter counts read-phase lifetimes and joins. It does not count reads or parses. The physical reads inside a phase appear under axm.parse.*, axm.io.* and axm.resolve.desired-state, and the resolve.desired-state span is emitted only inside a captured view (read-view.ts:284). Before the change, the same readers ran on live ports with no phase, so they produced no span here but parsed the documents once per reader.
explanations.mechanism:
The read-view primitive did not change. The rise comes from commits that wrap existing readers in a phase.

- In native-output-postconditions.ts, validateNativeOutputPostconditions runs its retention witnesses and required native-unit readback inside withFreshWorkspaceObservationReadView. It opens no phase when there are none.
- Result: two fresh phases per restored closure in the apply phase. The 50-package detail trace confirms it: 100 observation phases whose parent is operation.phase[apply], against 0 in old. That is +100, +20 and +2 in the sync-restore scenarios. It is also the likely source of the extra apply-phase phase in installed/enable, installed/skills-enable and typed/subagents/enable, and of the second apply phase in typed/{rules,knowledge,subagents}/new.

explanations.totals: Total count 60 -> 76 (+16). requested 60 -> 76, executed 60 -> 60, reused 0 -> 16. It rises in 16 scenarios, each by exactly 1 (1 -> 2): typed/{publish, skills, subagents, rules, packs, mcps, knowledge, hooks}/publish and preview/{publish, skills, subagents, rules, packs, mcps, knowledge, hooks}-publish. The worst case, typed/subagents/publish 1 -> 2, is the same size as every other rise. The 44 other scenarios that record the kind (install, update, view, migrate, demote, verify, startup checks) stay at 1. installed/adopt-enabled-native-refusal does not record this kind and is not involved.
explanations.whatIsCounted: One occurrence is one metadata request for one identity made through the in-invocation Registry read-phase cache. It is recorded by withWork("axm.registry.metadata-reuse", ...) in RegistryReadPhase.get in packages/supporting/registry-client/src/read-phase.ts, around line 154, with axm.work.requested=1. That recording code is the same at ada862c27 and 15cac0d07, so the counter's meaning did not change. Each occurrence's dimensions and counters say what happened. With axm.cache.outcome=miss and executed=1, this requester started the real lookup (the cache's lookup function ran, which for a file Registry is the batched index.json read under axm.registry.metadata-batch). With outcome hit or coalesced, executed=0 and reused=1, the answer came from the phase cache and no request or decode ran. So the kind counts lookups requested from the phase, whether executed or reused. The executed and reused fields tell real work apart from reuse hits.
explanations.mechanism: Commit 66ef873fc, "perf(registry): answer file Registry publication previews from the open read phase", causes the rise. Before it, the file Registry client's previewExtensionPublishes (packages/supporting/registry-client/src/local-client.ts) checked and read each target's and pack dependency's index.json directly with fs (registryPathExists + readExtensionIndex). That read was outside the read phase and was never counted under this kind. The commit adds LocalRegistryClientOptions.previewIndex. In packages/supporting/registry-client/src/registry-client-factory.ts, forEndpoint now passes a previewIndex that, while the read phase is open (new isOpen on the guarded phase), calls phase.get(endpoint, entry, selectionPolicy). That call is under the same key PublishExtensions.prepare used for its selectMany. phase.get always records one axm.registry.metadata-reuse occurrence. Because the selection's batch already holds the result, the preview's occurrence is outcome=hit, executed=0, reused=1. With no phase, or a phase that has ended, the preview still reads index.json itself. So in every file-Registry publish scenario, a direct read that was not counted became a counted cache hit, giving +1 occurrence per scenario.

explanations.whatIsCounted: axm.hash.content is a bounded WorkKind (packages/generic/host-primitives/src/work-observation.ts:67). One occurrence is one withWork span around executed hashing; axm.work.count is the number of items hashed and axm.work.bytes is the bytes hashed. It is executed work, not a reuse hit. In the old revision only one place recorded it: packages/core/workspace-kernel/src/workspace-state/workspace/rendered-files.ts:43. The change adds a second place, withSourceRevisions in packages/core/workspace-features/src/knowledge-query/knowledge-revision.ts. That span wraps the sha256 source revisions (computeKnowledgeSourceRevision) of a settled Knowledge corpus capture, with count = number of sources and bytes = their total size. In all five scenarios the new row comes from this place, owned by the KnowledgeDiscovery.* operation (for capabilities the owner is axm.cli.operation). No other scenario has a row with these 261 bytes.
explanations.mechanism:
The rise comes from commit 6a823aafd, "perf(knowledge): hash corpus sources once, after the confirming read", in packages/core/workspace-features/src/knowledge-query/knowledge-revision.ts.

- Old code: captureOnce computed computeKnowledgeSourceRevision(bytes) for every source, and it did so in both the capture read and the confirming read. captureKnowledgeCorpus also hashed the whole capture into a corpus fingerprint. None of this hashing was inside a withWork span. The old revision had no withWork import in knowledge-query, so the work was executed but recorded under no kind.
- New code: captureOnce only reads. After the byte compare succeeds, withSourceRevisions hashes the settled capture once, inside withWork("axm.hash.content", { count: captured.length, bytes }).

Commit ee72066b3 ("fingerprint a captured corpus once, in its index snapshot", knowledge-revision.ts and knowledge-index.ts makeKnowledgeIndexSnapshot) then removed the capture's unused corpus fingerprint. With one bundle, the snapshot now reuses the corpus fingerprint as the bundle fingerprint, so 3 fingerprint hashes become 1. Fingerprints are still uncounted under any kind.

Commits ddeac6394 and 74cbeb4a6 touch the same scenarios (manifest decode reuse, and one workspace read phase). They explain the fall in axm.io.read-file, axm.parse.* and axm.access, but not the hash row.

Net effect: the new counter makes visible a hash that already ran, and the amount of hashing behind it fell.

explanations.whatIsCounted:
These are kernel counters, not trace work. benchmarks/observability-physical-work.ts reduces one strace of an untraced invocation (the whole process tree) to per-path counters:
- openFailed: any open/openat that returns <0, including O_PATH opens.
- pathOpens: a successful O_PATH openat. Bun's realpath does this.
- directoryReads: a getdents64 call that returns >0, counted against the fd's path.
- stats: a stat, lstat or statx.
- access: an access/faccessat call. Effect's fs.exists does this.
Paths are projected to <ws>, <home>, <tmp> and so on. Temporary names are folded only when they match /\.tmp\.[0-9a-z]+\.[0-9a-z]+\.[0-9a-z]+$/ (".tmp.<atomic>"). A 12-hex suffix like axm.json.tmp.e8a5983ec9d6 does not match, so each run's random names appear as distinct paths. One occurrence is therefore one syscall on one path. A swap between syscall kinds (access -> failed open) or between names (old temp name -> new temp name) shows up as one counter rising and another falling.
explanations.mechanism:
(1) <tmp> in git/update is the host /tmp. Each Bun process (two per invocation, the same in both binaries) lists / and then /tmp at startup; this is runtime code, not product code. directoryOpens is 2->2. The /tmp listing spans about 9400 shared host entries: the baseline's second process read 9411 entries in 54 non-empty getdents64 batches, the candidate's read 9412 in 55. That is one more batch only because the shared host /tmp changed size. getdents64 totals fell 542->533.

(2) Upgrade realpaths its own executable once. The old binary's path .../binaries/final-baseline/axm-linux-x64 goes pathOpens 1->0 and the candidate's .../binaries/candidate-15cac0d07/axm-linux-x64 goes 0->1. Net 0.

(3) Commit ea5e12097 ('reuse prepared pack manifests, read hook metadata once'), in packages/core/workspace-features/src/authoring/hooks/interchange.ts. The function prepareNativeHookImport used to run fs.exists(hook-bundle.json) and then read the file. It now calls readOptionalMetadata, which reads once, treats NotFound as absence, and probes only on other failures. For the absent file, the access becomes a failed O_RDONLY open: access 1->0, openFailed 0->1. Commit 9150d2c12 also removed a second realPath of the root (<ws>/native pathOpens 2->1).

(4) Commit fcf4471d9 ('read the update-check cache and install metadata once'), in packages/supporting/cli-maintenance/src/self-update/adapters/native/update-cache/index.ts. makeUpdateCheckCache.read changed from exists+readFileString to readFileStringIfPresent. For the missing cache file: access 1->0, openFailed 0->1.

(5) Commit 5907df664 ('read a sourced connection's manifest without a prior probe'), in packages/core/workspace-kernel/src/projection/mcps/inspection.ts, function findManifestRoot. For each canonical root it now tries readFileStringIfPresent(<root>/mcp.json) first, and keeps the old fs.exists probe only when the read fails for a reason other than NotFound. That fallback preserves the old diagnostic and failure precedence, as the commit message states. One candidate root in these scenarios is the file <ws>/.mcp.json. Its read attempt resolves the path first, as an O_PATH realpath, which fails with ENOTDIR. ENOTDIR is not NotFound, so the retained access probe still runs (access 1->1). The result is one new failed open: openFailed 0->1, plus a new io.real-path trace row with failure.kind=failure (count 1) in axm.observation.phase. For the real package root, the read replaces probe-plus-read, so both scenarios fall overall.

(6) Both binaries write the same two staged files, axm.json and axm.lock, under random 12-hex suffixes that the projection does not fold. The old names (axm.json.tmp.54dacddf6b6d, axm.lock.tmp.0415c04b2469) fall by exactly the amounts the new names rise: 213 and 601 bytes, stats 3, one read and one write each.

(7) After writes, the archive cache's automatic prune (packages/supporting/registry-client/src/archive-cache.ts) lists <home>/.cache/axm/archives and stats every archive present at that moment. directoryOpens is 2->2 for 10 archives and 12->12 for 50. How many prune passes see an archive depends on when its concurrent download, slowed by the fixture's 100 ms archive-body delay, gets renamed into place. In the 10-archive case the baseline's second prune listed the directory just before nmC_ was renamed; the candidate's listed it just after. Neither recent commit to archive-cache.ts (51bc21ce4, d92264013) touches pruning.

(8) maps: Bun reads /proc/self/maps once per process. The candidate's directory name is 5 characters longer (candidate-15cac0d07 has 19, final-baseline has 14), and the binary path appears on 6 mappings. That gives +30 bytes per process (181 scenarios) or +60 for two processes (77). The two outliers differ by one anonymous mapping line of about 49 bytes: maintenance/changed -19 and typed/hooks/test +79. statm and cpu/online are read by the runtime: memory and GC sampling, and thread-pool sizing. Product code contains no memoryUsage, statm or cpus calls. They follow runtime activity and wall time, and fall overall.

verdicts.subject: trace kind axm.observation.reuse: 146,877 -> 222,437, rising in 5 scenarios; worst registry/50/sync-restore/cold/baseline 46,622 -> 129,432
concerns: Mechanism checked against the code. In c4f23d1be, runMaterializeOperation's validate step wraps manager.isInstalled in withFreshWorkspaceObservationReadView (operations.ts:1011 at 15cac0d07). validateNativeOutputPostconditions moves the retention-witness check, observeNativeOutputs and the instruction readback into one fresh view, and returns early only when both retained and required are empty. share() in observation-read-view.ts records one axm.observation.reuse span per request. A miss runs the wrapped live fs call once, a hit or coalesced request reuses the stored result, and bypass goes to the live fs. Nothing in the capture path reads ahead or prefetches, so a view adds no reads of its own. One caveat: decode-text is shared over io.readFileString, which goes through the shared readFile, so one physical document read records two miss spans (decode-text and read-file). That is double counting inside this counter, not double I/O.

Re-measured the cited scenarios registry/50 cold, registry/10 cold, installed/enable, installed/skills-enable and typed/subagents/enable. The uncited ones were registry/1/sync-restore/warm, path/cold-sync, git/cold-sync and typed/subagents/update. Every axm.io.* kind falls in every scenario where reuse changes, and parse.settings and parse.lockfile fall too. Per-path kernel scan of all nine scenarios: no workspace, native-output, settings or lockfile path gains a readOpen, stat, readlink, access or directory read. The only rises are /proc/<pid>/statm and /proc/<pid>/maps runtime polling, plus one cache archive .zip whose stats go 3->4 (registry/50) or 1->2 (registry/10). In both cases every archive .tmp file loses a stat (1->0), so the archive cache loses stats overall. Treated as cache-ordering noise, not added work.

The rise of this counter cannot be split from the other commits in the aggregates (canonical-path memoisation, 869f3c5ae, ceeed0a72, 9b3f55f79). c4f23d1be's own physical effect is shown only by the per-path kernel counts and falling totals, not one to one. That span exists only inside a captured phase (read-view.ts:284), so evaluations that used to run on live readers were never counted; parse.settings 508->306 and parse.lockfile 606->256 fall at the same time. axm.render.native goes 0->6, with workCount 0 on every row.
